memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He shall also burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar. The man who releases the goat as a scapegoat must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may come into the camp." - Lev 16:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even the man who led the goat away had to wash before coming home.

He had done nothing wrong. He was obeying instructions, performing a necessary service. But he had handled what carried the sin of a nation, and he did not walk straight back into the camp as though nothing had happened.

There is wisdom here for anyone who serves others in difficult places. Pastors who sit with people in their worst moments. Counsellors, doctors, social workers, police. Those who care for the dying. Anyone who works close to human brokenness.

You cannot handle that and be unaffected. It marks you. And if you do not attend to it, you carry it home to people who did not ask for it.

Notice that God builds the washing into the instructions. He does not treat this man's need as weakness or lack of faith. It is simply what handling sin does to a person, and God makes provision for it.

Even Jesus withdrew regularly to lonely places to pray (Luke 5:16) — after the crowds, after the demands, after carrying what others brought Him.

If you serve in hard places, do not skip the washing. It is not optional.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you carry the weight of others' burdens without attending to it?
2. What is your equivalent of washing before you come back into the camp?
3. Who serves you in hard places and needs care themselves?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You make provision for those who serve in difficult places. Teach me to bring what I carry to You, and not to take it home unwashed. Amen.
